intended_object: The set of characteristic covectors of the plumbing lattice ℤ^V: integral covectors k with k(x) ≡ x·x (mod 2) for all lattice vectors x, equivalently k(E_v) ≡ e_v (mod 2) for every vertex v. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Némethi's lattice homology.
explanation: The definition is the subtype of k : V → ℤ with k v ≡ P.weight v [ZMOD 2] for every vertex v. P.weight v is the self-intersection E_v·E_v of the basis sphere. For x = Σ a_v E_v, x·x ≡ Σ a_v E_v·E_v (mod 2): the cross terms are even and a² ≡ a mod 2. So the vertex-wise condition is equivalent to the usual k(x) ≡ x·x (mod 2) for all x, and the library proves this equivalence (isCharacteristicVector_iff_forall_modEq_intersectionForm). Representing covectors by their values V → ℤ on the basis matches Hom(ℤ^V, ℤ). The notion is specific to the integral plumbing lattice, so the setting is natural, not too narrow. I found no Mathlib definition of characteristic vectors of an integral bilinear form.
